sections.Highlights: THIS... is a 1991 Lamborghini Diablo, finished in white with a black and red interior, and offered by AutoCentroImports, a Cars & Bids Certified Seller. This Diablo is a left-hand drive, Italian-spec coupe equipped with a gated 5-speed manual that has reportedly been restored and upgraded with components from Diablo GT, SV, SVR, 6.0, and SE30 models, among other modifications detailed below. The selling dealer notes that the driver's door jamb was autographed by Valentino Balboni in November 2024. Documentation in the gallery indicates that this Lamborghini underwent recent extensive maintenance at Evans Automotive Repair in Columbus, Ohio, totaling over $124k. Notable services include an engine and transmission rebuild, clutch, and timing chain and water pump replacement, among others detailed below. This Lamborghini was reportedly imported from Japan, and is currently titled in Virginia as a 1992 model. It's equipped with a metric instrument cluster, and its odometer displays about 26,500 kilometers, which represents approximately 16,500 miles. The attached Carfax vehicle history report begins in 2018 and contains multiple reporting gaps, though it shows no accidents or mileage discrepancies during the given time period. Launched as the replacement for the iconic Countach, the Lamborghini Diablo had big shoes to fill. Though its architecture was similar to its predecessor's, the Diablo received a wider stance and a longer wheelbase for improved drivability and increased cabin space. It was also the first regular-production Lamborghini to reach a top speed of over 200 mph. Production ran from 1990 to 2001, with multiple versions and revisions along the way. Power comes from a 5.7-liter V12. The seller reports that this Diablo currently produces approximately 575 horsepower according to George Evans of Evans Automotive Repair, but a dyno sheet was not provided to confirm. Output is sent to the rear wheels via a gated 5-speed manual transmission.
sections.Equipment: A partial list of notable currently installed equipment reported by the selling dealer includes: 18-inch OZ Racing Diablo SV wheels with Pirelli P Zero tires Al Burtoni Diablo SE30 Jota air intake system (including dual intake engine bonnet roof scoops and a custom throttle body system) Custom sport exhaust system from Japan Kevlar clutch kit KONI dampers Diablo GT body components Diablo 6.0 headlights Diablo SV-R rear wing Rear bumper delete Carbon taillight bezels, rockers, and hood Repainted white (when imported to the U.S. in 2018) Scissor doors Leather upholstery Air conditioning Custom instrument cluster Center console gauges Custom red floor mats
sections.Seller Notes: Since this Diablo is an imported vehicle, it may not pass emissions testing in some states. As always, it's the buyer's responsibility to perform all due diligence regarding registering this Diablo in their respective state prior to placing a bid. The selling dealer reports that this Lamborghini was repainted in white over the factory red when it was imported to the U.S. in 2018.
